speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you had a rear-end collision and are now experiencing right groin pain with an abnormal leg position. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly how you were positioned in the vehicle at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture.

Given your history of being the restrained driver in a rear-end collision, immediate onset of right groin pain, and abnormal leg positioning, a femoral neck fracture is the most likely diagnosis. I will proceed to confirm this with a X-Ray of your right hip. REQUEST TEST: Right_Hip_XRay.
